title: Professional TypeScript Best Practices knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a production-oriented TypeScript project demonstrate?
options: A working happy path without tests or documentation.
Secrets committed into client bundles for convenience.
Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
Type annotations as a replacement for authorization and validation.
questions.answer_key: Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
questions.explanation: Production readiness requires runtime, security, testing and operational evidence beyond type checking.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Professional TypeScript Best Practices”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with prefer precise types and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with prefer precise types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Prefer precise types”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Professional TypeScript Best Practices”?
options: Check use runtime validation at trust boundaries, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume keep type definitions understandable and maintainable is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check use runtime validation at trust boundaries, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Use runtime validation at trust boundaries”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
